data.body:
ESCALATION (autonomous agent, not claimed): deferring implementation — unsettled security/trust-model design decisions.

I analyzed this STORY against the current code and ADRs (0043/0044/0045/0046/0049 on the attestation/op-cert model, 0013/0020 two-vote merge gate, 0088 code-review novelty convergence). Two things block a safe autonomous implementation.

1) The identity-scoping premise for COMPLETION is already satisfied — please confirm intent.
- `_reusable_attested_pass` (close_autoresume.py) reuses ONLY an op-cert for which `signing.verify_signature(kind="completion-verifier")` returns `verified: True` + `opcert: True`.
- `_opcert_signing.verify_opcert_record` returns `verified: True` ONLY when `record.principal == own_principal` (else verdict `foreign_key`, not certified) AND the DSSE signature verifies under THIS environment's OWN public key (`_opcert_own_public_key`). A spoofed plaintext principal fails the signature check under own_pub.
- Therefore completion reuse is ALREADY identity-scoped by construction: a local-dev cert is already rejected by the AWS bot (foreign principal / signature not under own key) and vice-versa. The AC's "make completion reuse identity-scoped" is effectively a documentation + explicit-test task, NOT a trust-model change. If the intent is instead a DIFFERENT identity notion (e.g. key-fingerprint vs `env_id`/`REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID` principal, or pinned trusted-environment identity), that is a new decision — please specify which.

2) The CODE-REVIEW attestation reuse is genuinely NEW security infrastructure with unsettled design — DECISIONS NEEDED:
- No code-review op-cert exists today. The only op-cert `kind` slots are `plan-review` and `completion-verifier`. The code-review gate PRODUCES the Gerrit `LLM-Review` vote and only CONSUMES a plan-review attestation (bugfix_size_gate.classify_plan_review_attestation); it signs nothing itself. So "review-code RECORDS/SIGNS a reusable code-review attestation" requires deciding the new attestation kind slot and its policy entry.
- No material fingerprint over a REVIEW INPUT (a diff/ref) exists. `plan_review.attest.current_material_fingerprint` is ticket-state-based. The AC's "same-`ref` … material fingerprint that still match the review input" needs a newly-defined, authenticated diff/ref fingerprint. What exactly does a code-review attestation bind — {ticket_id, base..head range, diff content hash, merged_log_commit}? This is undefined.
- `review-code` is diff-oriented (`--base/--head/--diff-file/--ref`), not ticket-oriented (no `ticket_id` arg). "RECORD its result ON THE TICKET" requires deciding how a review resolves/binds to a ticket (via the change's `rebar-ticket:` trailer?) and how that composes with the existing ADR 0088 `code-review: session:<id>` convergence artifact (which is a separate, unsigned finding-memory mechanism, NOT an op-cert).
- Merge-gate trust boundary (ADR 0013/0020): whether a REUSED code-review attestation may satisfy the `LLM-Review +1` vote — and across which environments — is a merge-gate trust decision with no governing ADR. Reuse that short-circuits a fresh LLM review at merge time changes what the `LLM-Review` label attests.

3) The shared reuse seam (AC #3) is an engineering decision I can make during implementation, but it depends on (2) being settled first (there is no second reuse implementation to unify with until the code-review producer/consumer shape is decided).

Recommendation: record the decisions above in a short ADR (or here) — (a) confirm/clarify the identity notion for reuse; (b) define the code-review op-cert kind + its {ref/diff material} binding; (c) how review-code binds to a ticket and composes with ADR 0088; (d) whether a reused code-review attestation may satisfy the LLM-Review merge vote and under what identity scope. Then this STORY can be implemented (likely split: completion identity-scoping test coverage + shared-seam refactor as one change; the new code-review producer/consumer as another) under the plan-review/close gates.

Leaving the ticket UNCLAIMED and as-is (status open). No code changed. No force used.
